precepts.text: If the Most High cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.
precepts.point: But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, so there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.” If the Most High cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you. That kingdom is the answer to Eliphaz. He asks, “Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or is it gain to him, that thou makest thy ways perfect?”, throwing Job's righteousness back as filthy rags, as if keeping the commandments profits nothing.

But there is a kingdom of God that comes, and Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him. So there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

precepts.text: Dare any of you go to law before the unjust and not the saints? Do you not know that the saints shall judge the world?
precepts.point: But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, so there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints? Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world? and if the world shall be judged by you, are ye unworthy to judge the smallest matters?” The saints shall judge the world.

That is what righteousness profits. Eliphaz asks, “Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise may be profitable unto himself?” and “Will he reprove thee for fear of thee? will he enter with thee into judgment?”, as if keeping the commandments profits nothing. But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, and the saints shall judge the world. There is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

precepts.text: Those who followed Christ in the regeneration shall sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
precepts.point: But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, so there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
Peter asked it plainly: “Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore?” And Christ answered, “Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” Those who followed Christ, in the regeneration, sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

So it is not true that there is no gain to a man in making his ways perfect. Eliphaz throws Job's righteousness back as filthy rags, asking “Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous?” But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him. There is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

precepts.text: If the wicked turn from all his sins and keep the statutes, he shall surely live, and his transgressions shall not be mentioned unto him.
precepts.point: But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, so there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“But if the wicked will turn from all his sins that he hath committed, and keep all my statutes, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live, he shall not die. All his transgressions that he hath committed, they shall not be mentioned unto him: in his righteousness that he hath done he shall live.” Keeping the statutes profits: it is life, and the transgressions are not mentioned.

Eliphaz says, “Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?”, as if righteousness gains a man nothing before the Almighty. But the Most High says the man that turns and keeps all his statutes shall surely live, in his righteousness that he hath done. So keeping the commandments is not filthy rags, and there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

precepts.text: Whatsoever was written aforetime was written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope, even when men call us a hate group.
precepts.point: But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, so there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Eliphaz's answer to Job was written for our learning. Men throw our righteousness back at us as filthy rags, as if keeping the commandments profits nothing, and call us a hate group, the way Eliphaz asked Job, “Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous?”

Through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope, even when men call us a hate group: Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him. So there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer, and the scriptures give us the hope he tried to take from Job.

precepts.text: Nineveh proclaimed a fast, man and beast covered in sackcloth, crying mightily unto God and turning from evil.
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
Nineveh proclaimed a fast “by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.” Man and beast covered in sackcloth, crying mightily unto God and turning from evil.

Eliphaz claims Job's suffering proves Job was sinning, that snares are round about him and sudden fear troubles him because he stripped the naked and withheld bread from the hungry. But the Lord was only trying him. Nineveh shows what a people do when they are truly in sin: they turn from their evil way. The truth is the opposite of what Eliphaz says: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

precepts.text: Who can tell if God will turn and repent? No man can tell you the Most High will not forgive you when you change.
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?” No man can tell you the Most High will not forgive you when you change. Nineveh did not know whether God would turn, but they turned from their evil way anyway, and left it to him.

Eliphaz has it backwards: he claims Job's suffering proves Job was sinning, and that therefore snares are round about him and sudden fear troubles him. But the Lord was only trying him. When Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city. No man can tell what the Most High will do with a man, and no man could tell Job he was under fierce anger for sin he did not commit.

precepts.text: Is not destruction to the wicked? Doth not he see my ways and count all my steps?
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity? Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?” Job knows destruction is to the wicked, and he knows the Most High sees his ways and counts all his steps. So he does not fear the accounting Eliphaz tries to lay on him.

Eliphaz accuses him of taking a pledge from his brother for naught, stripping the naked of their clothing, withholding water from the weary and bread from the hungry, sending widows away empty, and breaking the arms of the fatherless, and says that is why snares are round about him. But the Lord was only trying him. The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city, and God counted every one of those steps.

precepts.text: If Job walked with vanity or deceit, let another eat what he sowed and his offspring be rooted out.
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
Job answers the accusation with his own oath: “If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit; Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity.” “If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands; Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.” If Job walked with vanity or deceit, let another eat what he sowed and his offspring be rooted out.

That is not the answer of a man who stripped the naked of their clothing and withheld bread from the hungry, as Eliphaz claims. Eliphaz says Job's suffering proves Job was sinning, but the Lord was only trying him. When Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city, and he asks to be weighed in an even balance to prove it.

precepts.text: If Job's heart was deceived by a woman or he laid wait at his neighbor's door, let his wife grind unto another; Job shows he dealt righteously.
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door; Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.” If Job's heart was deceived by a woman or he laid wait at his neighbor's door, let his wife grind unto another. Job shows he dealt righteously; he lays his own wife on the line against the charge.

So Eliphaz's claim that snares are round about Job and sudden fear troubles him because he sent widows away empty and broke the arms of the fatherless does not stand. Eliphaz claims Job's suffering proves Job was sinning, but the Lord was only trying him. The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

precepts.text: Thunders, lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mount, and the trumpet exceeding loud, when the people met with God.
precepts.point: Thick clouds are a covering to him that he seeth not, and he walketh in the circuit of heaven. Eliphaz says God is surrounded by thick clouds and cannot judge through them, but that is when God is really looking, when you think he is not.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled.” Thunders, lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mount, and the trumpet exceeding loud, when the people met with God.

Eliphaz says “Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not”, as if God is surrounded by thick clouds and cannot judge through them. But the thick cloud on the mount was where God was, and the people trembled before it. The thick cloud is not a covering that keeps him from seeing; that is when God is really looking, when you think he is not.

precepts.text: The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.
precepts.point: Thick clouds are a covering to him that he seeth not, and he walketh in the circuit of heaven. Eliphaz says God is surrounded by thick clouds and cannot judge through them, but that is when God is really looking, when you think he is not.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why: “The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.” Eliphaz asks, “How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?”, and says thick clouds are a covering to him that he seeth not. But the eyes of the Lord are in every place. There is no dark cloud he cannot judge through; he beholds the evil and the good. That is when God is really looking, when you think he is not.

precepts.text: The Lord is in his holy temple, his throne is in heaven; his eyes behold, his eyelids try the children of men.
precepts.point: Thick clouds are a covering to him that he seeth not, and he walketh in the circuit of heaven. Eliphaz says God is surrounded by thick clouds and cannot judge through them, but that is when God is really looking, when you think he is not.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“The Lord is in his holy temple, the Lord’s throne is in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men.” Eliphaz says, “Is not God in the height of heaven?”, and then that thick clouds are a covering to him so that he seeth not, and he walketh in the circuit of heaven. The Lord's throne is in heaven, yes, but from there his eyes behold and his eyelids try the children of men.

So the height of heaven is no distance from his judgment. He is not walking the circuit of heaven blind behind the clouds; that is when God is really looking, when you think he is not.

precepts.point: Receive the law from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty you shall be built up and put away iniquity far from your tabernacle. This was our job, to build up our people.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
Eliphaz tells Job, “Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.” You do not acquaint yourself with God by whispering that you love him. You hear from God through his prophets and his people to whom he gave his word, and Ecclesiasticus shows how that is done: “My son, if thou wilt, thou shalt be taught: and if thou wilt apply thy mind, thou shalt be prudent. If thou love to hear, thou shalt receive understanding: and if thou bow thine ear, thou shalt be wise”.

It means putting yourself where the word is taught. “Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave unto him that is wise. Be willing to hear every godly discourse; and let not the parables of understanding escape thee.” When you see a man of understanding, “get thee betimes unto him, and let thy foot wear the steps of his door.”

That is how you “Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.” “Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.” Being acquainted with the Most High is hearing his law from his people and laying it up in the heart; that is where the peace and the good begin.

precepts.point: Receive the law from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty you shall be built up and put away iniquity far from your tabernacle. This was our job, to build up our people.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint thyself with their proverbs: for of them thou shalt learn instruction, and how to serve great men with ease.” The same word Eliphaz uses: acquaint. You acquaint yourself with God by acquainting yourself with the discourse of the wise, his prophets and his people to whom he gave his word, not by whispering that you love him.

“Miss not the discourse of the elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them thou shalt learn understanding, and to give answer as need requireth.” The word came down from the fathers to the elders, and from the elders to us. That is receiving the law from his mouth and laying up his words in the heart.

precepts.text: Set over the nations to root out, pull down, destroy, throw down, build up, and plant the seeds of God's word in his people.
precepts.point: Receive the law from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty you shall be built up and put away iniquity far from your tabernacle. This was our job, to build up our people.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up”. Jeremiah was told, “See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.”

That was our job: to build up our people. Set over the nations to root out, pull down, destroy and throw down, and then to build up and plant the seeds of God's word in his people. Returning to the Almighty is how a people is built up and puts iniquity far from its tabernacles.
